instructions:
PostFast schedules and publishes social posts across X, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, Telegram, and Google Business Profile.

Flow: list_accounts (+ list_workspaces) to see what's connected → create_posts (one socialMediaId per post; batch up to 15) → attach media via upload_from_url (a public https URL) or upload_media (base64 bytes in data + contentType). Posts are held for approval and nothing publishes until approve_posts sets them to APPROVED: show the user what will be posted, where and when, and call approve_posts only after they say yes, even if they asked you to post it.

Workspaces: omit workspaceId to use the connection's default; pass a workspaceId (from list_workspaces) to act in another workspace.

Before scheduling, confirm the target account's connectionStatus is CONNECTED. A DISABLED account will not publish (disconnected accounts are the #1 cause of failed posts) — saving a DRAFT is still allowed.

Status & timing: status=SCHEDULED requires scheduledAt on every post (ISO-8601, in the future, within 1 year); status=DRAFT must omit scheduledAt. Every post is created as PENDING_APPROVAL and publishes at its scheduledAt only once approve_posts sets it to APPROVED.

Media: use the key returned by an upload tool, and set mediaItems[].type to match the file (IMAGE for image/* keys, VIDEO for video/* keys — a mismatch is rejected). Videos are capped at 250MB (Telegram 50MB, Bluesky 100MB). Media is REQUIRED on TikTok, YouTube (video only), Instagram, and Pinterest; X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky, Telegram, and Google Business Profile allow text-only posts (GBP accepts 1 image and no video). This requirement applies even to DRAFTS — a draft to a media-required platform without media is rejected. So if the user asks to post to a media-required platform and provides no media, ask them for an image/video (or generate and upload one) BEFORE calling create_posts; don't attempt the post without media.

Per-platform limits (media counts / characters):
- X: up to 4 images or 1 video (no mixing); 280 chars (4,000 with X Premium).
- TikTok: 1 video OR up to 10 images; 4,000 chars.
- Instagram: up to 10 media items, images and videos mixed; 2,200 chars, max 5 hashtags.
- YouTube: 1 video, no images; title max 100 chars.
- Facebook / LinkedIn: up to 10 images OR 1 video (no mixing).
- Threads: up to 10 media items, images and videos mixed; 500 chars.
- Pinterest: up to 5 images or 1 video; title max 100, description max 800.
- Google Business Profile: text only, or 1 image and no video; 1,500 chars.
- Bluesky: up to 10 images or 1 video. Telegram: up to 10 media items, at most 3 of them videos.
No post carries more than 10 media items.
If content exceeds the target platform's character limit, don't schedule it as-is — tell the user and offer to shorten or split it (X is 280 unless the account has X Premium = 4,000).

Platform-specific options go in the controls object, e.g.:
- Pinterest: controls.pinterestBoardId is REQUIRED — it is a board's boardId from list_pinterest_boards, NOT the Pinterest account's socialMediaId.
- Google Business Profile: controls.gbpLocationId is required — the locationId from list_gbp_locations.
- YouTube: controls.youtubePlaylistId is the playlistId from list_youtube_playlists; youtubeIsShort defaults true; title falls back to the first 100 chars of content; youtubeLanguage sets the video's language (BCP-47, e.g. en-GB) and youtubeCaptionKey adds an uploaded .srt/.vtt caption file in that language (never in mediaItems).
- TikTok: controls.tiktokPrivacy is deprecated (videos use the account default, photos default to public); tiktokTitle applies to photo carousels only (max 90); firstComment (max 1,200).
- Instagram: controls.instagramPublishType = TIMELINE | STORY | REEL.
- Facebook: controls.facebookContentType = POST | REEL | STORY. controls.facebookTargetCountries limits who can see a FEED post by country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, max 25; not Reels/Stories).
- Geotag a place (Facebook/Instagram): call search_places, then pass a returned id as controls.facebookPlaceId (Facebook feed posts only — not Reels/Stories/video) and/or controls.instagramLocationId (Instagram single media only — not carousels). One id works for both.
- LinkedIn: to attach a PDF, Word or PowerPoint document (shown as pages readers swipe through), upload it, then pass its key as controls.linkedinAttachmentKey (never in mediaItems, and not with images or a video on the same post) and its title as controls.linkedinAttachmentTitle.
- X: controls.xRetweetUrl reposts an existing tweet (content/media are ignored).
Note: list_pinterest_boards / list_youtube_playlists / list_gbp_locations take the account's socialMediaId; each returned item has BOTH an internal id and the platform id (boardId / playlistId / locationId) — pass the PLATFORM id to controls, not the internal id or the account id.

Failed posts carry lastError — usually a disconnected account (reconnect, then retry) or platform-rejected media.

delete_post (one post) and delete_posts (up to 100 in one call) remove posts from PostFast only — they never delete an already-published post from the social platform. Say so when a user asks to delete something that has already gone out. Deleting can't be undone, so show the user which posts (account, time, first line) and call delete_post or delete_posts only after they say yes in the conversation.

Social inbox (comments on your posts: TikTok, Instagram, Facebook Pages, Threads; an account's inboxCapable flag from list_accounts says what is live today): read with list_inbox_conversations → list_inbox_items (get_inbox_unread_count for the total). A public reply under a comment, an Instagram private reply (one per comment, within 7 days) and a permanent comment deletion each take two tools: preview it with preview_comment_reply, preview_private_reply or preview_comment_deletion, show the user the preview, and carry it out with reply_to_comment, send_private_reply or delete_comment only after they say yes, even if they gave you the text. Whether and how long a reply can be comes ONLY from the conversation's server-computed canReply / maxReplyLength / windowState / disabledReason; never assume platform rules. Hide or restore a comment with set_inbox_item_state (HIDE / UNHIDE), triage with set_inbox_conversation_status and assign_inbox_conversation, and call mark_inbox_conversation_read after presenting a thread. It is a comments inbox; never present it as DMs or messages.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.title: List Posts
tools.description: List social media posts with optional filters for specific IDs, accounts, platform, status, and date range. Failed or missed posts carry a lastError { message, code }; codes include MISSED_DISCONNECTED (the account was disconnected when the post was due — reconnect, then retry) and MISSED_NOT_PUBLISHED (passed its scheduled time plus a 2h grace window without publishing). Each post also carries controls { threadsTopicTag, instagramPublishType, facebookContentType, tiktokIsDraft, youtubePrivacy }, each null when unset. Only the field for the post's own platform (its account's platform in list_accounts) is meaningful: posts created through the API store every platform's defaults, so the other fields can be non-null.

ids.description: Fetch only these post ids (workspace-scoped; max 100; AND-ed with other filters)

socialMediaIds.description: Only posts on these accounts (ids from list_accounts; max 100; AND-ed with other filters)

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: create_posts
tools.title: Create Posts
tools.description: Create social media posts (batch up to 15), held for approval: nothing publishes until approve_posts sets them to APPROVED. Each post targets one social account (socialMediaId from list_accounts). SCHEDULED requires scheduledAt on every post; DRAFT must omit scheduledAt. Scheduling to a disconnected account (connectionStatus DISABLED in list_accounts) is rejected with HTTP 400 "socialMediaDisconnected" — pre-check connectionStatus before calling. Saving as DRAFT to a disconnected account is allowed. TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and Pinterest require at least one media item EVEN FOR DRAFTS — attach media first (ask the user for an image/video, or generate+upload one, if none was provided). Google Business Profile accepts text-only posts, or one image and no video. A post carries at most 10 media items. Attach media via the key returned by upload_from_url / upload_media. A Threads post can carry one topic, set with controls.threadsTopicTag; like every control it applies to every post in the call, so put Threads posts with different topics in separate calls.

firstComment.description: First comment posted automatically after publishing. Supported on X, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Threads, and TikTok (TikTok: max 1,200 chars).

key.description: Media key from upload_from_url / upload_media (e.g. image/<uuid>.jpg)

coverImageKey.description: Media key of a custom cover/thumbnail for video posts. Supported on Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels, Pinterest video pins, and TikTok videos.

coverTimestamp.description: Video cover timestamp in milliseconds (e.g. "5000" = 5s). Fallback when coverImageKey is also provided.

scheduledAt.description: Schedule time (ISO 8601). Required when status is SCHEDULED.

status.description: Post status. SCHEDULED requires scheduledAt on every post.

approvalStatus.description: Posts created here are always held for approval. Publish them with approve_posts after the user confirms.

controls.description: Platform-specific controls (shared across all posts in the batch)

tiktokPrivacy.description: Deprecated. TikTok videos use the account default privacy (no per-post control) and photos default to public; use a draft for private posts.

tiktokAutoAddMusic.description: Let TikTok add a recommended sound. Photo/carousel posts only (ignored on videos). Mutually exclusive with tiktokMusicSoundId (sending both is rejected).

tiktokIsAigc.description: Declare the post as AI-generated content (videos and photo posts). Instagram's equivalent is instagramIsAiGenerated, YouTube's is youtubeContainsSyntheticMedia.

tiktokTitle.description: Title for TikTok photo posts (max 90 chars; photo posts only). When set, the full post content becomes the description; without it, content auto-splits on the first newline into title + description.

tiktokMusicSoundId.description: Commercial Music Library sound id from list_tiktok_sounds. TikTok photo, carousel and video posts. On videos the track plays at 50% volume over the video's original audio at 50%, like the TikTok app; there are no volume or trim controls. Mutually exclusive with tiktokAutoAddMusic (sending both is rejected). Not applied when tiktokIsDraft is true. Omit for no sound.

tiktokMusicSoundName.description: Display label for the chosen sound, e.g. 'Ok I Like It — Milky Chance'. Stored for the composer UI only; set it whenever tiktokMusicSoundId is set.

instagramTrialReelStrategy.description: Publish as an Instagram trial reel — shown only to non-followers until it graduates to your followers. MANUAL: you graduate it yourself in the Instagram app. SS_PERFORMANCE: Instagram graduates it automatically if it performs well. Requires instagramPublishType REEL (otherwise rejected with HTTP 400 "instagram.trialReelOnlyForReels") and cannot be combined with instagramCollaborators ("instagram.trialReelNoCollaborators"). Omit for a normal reel.

instagramLocationId.description: Geotag a single-media IG post — a numeric Facebook Page id with location data from search_places (same id as facebookPlaceId). Image/video/reel/story only, NOT carousels.

instagramLocationName.description: Display-only place label from search_places (stored for your portal; never sent to Meta)

instagramIsAiGenerated.description: Adds Instagram's 'AI info' label to the post — set it when the image or video was AI-generated. Applies to images, reels, stories and carousels; on a carousel it labels the whole post, not individual slides. Set at creation only: the label cannot be added or removed after publishing. TikTok's equivalent is tiktokIsAigc, YouTube's is youtubeContainsSyntheticMedia.

youtubeContainsSyntheticMedia.description: Discloses that the video contains realistic altered or synthetic (AI) content. Sent to YouTube only when true. Set at creation only. Instagram's equivalent is instagramIsAiGenerated, TikTok's is tiktokIsAigc.

youtubePlaylistId.description: YouTube playlist id — the playlistId field from list_youtube_playlists

youtubeThumbnailKey.description: Media key for a custom YouTube thumbnail (JPEG or PNG image, up to 10 MB, at least 640 px wide, 16:9 (1280x720 or larger))

youtubeLanguage.description: The video's language as a BCP-47 code, e.g. en, en-GB, es, es-419, fr, fr-CA, pt-BR or zh-Hans. Sets both YouTube's Video language (what is spoken) and its Title and description language, and is the language of the youtubeCaptionKey captions. An unknown code is rejected with HTTP 400 "youtubeLanguage.invalid". Used only by YouTube posts; applies to every post in this call, so put videos in different languages in separate calls.

youtubeCaptionKey.description: Captions for the video: the media_id (file/<uuid>.srt or .vtt) that upload_media or upload_from_url returns for an .srt or .vtt caption file (contentType application/x-subrip or text/vtt). Upload the file before this call, and never put its key in mediaItems. It becomes the video's caption track in the language set by youtubeLanguage, which is required with it (otherwise HTTP 400 "youtubeCaptionKey.languageRequired"); one caption track per post. The file must be a timed SRT or WebVTT file (each caption with its start --> end time), plain UTF-8 text, at most 10 MB; a transcript without timings doesn't work. YouTube's automatic captions stay listed separately as "(auto-generated)". If adding the captions fails, the video still publishes, without them. Used only by YouTube posts; applies to every post in this call, so each video with its own caption file needs its own create_posts call.

facebookTargetCountries.description: Limit who can see a Facebook FEED post by country — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (case-insensitive), max 25. Audience gating (hidden from everyone else), feed posts only — not Reels/Stories/video.

facebookPlaceId.description: Geotag a Facebook FEED post — a numeric Facebook Page id with location data from search_places (same id as instagramLocationId). Feed posts only (text/photo/carousel) — not Reels/Stories/video.

facebookPlaceName.description: Display-only place label from search_places (stored for your portal; never sent to Meta)

gbpLocationId.description: GBP location resource name — the locationId field from list_gbp_locations

gbpCallToActionUrl.description: CTA button URL (not needed for CALL, ignored for OFFER)

pinterestBoardId.description: Pinterest board id — the boardId field from list_pinterest_boards (NOT the account's socialMediaId)

linkedinAttachmentKey.description: A document for LinkedIn posts: a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file, at most 60 MB, which LinkedIn shows in the post as pages readers swipe through. Pass the media_id (file/<uuid>.pdf, .doc, .docx, .ppt or .pptx) that upload_media or upload_from_url returns as type DOCUMENT. Upload the file before this call, and never put its key in mediaItems. A LinkedIn post has either this document or mediaItems, never both: a post with both fails to publish. Set linkedinAttachmentTitle with it. Used only by LinkedIn posts; applies to every LinkedIn post in this call, so a LinkedIn post with images, a video or a different document needs its own create_posts call.

linkedinAttachmentTitle.description: The title shown with the linkedinAttachmentKey document in the LinkedIn post; without one, the post shows the title "Document". Used only with linkedinAttachmentKey.

threadsTopicTag.description: Threads topic for the post: one topic, not a list; 1-50 characters, no '.' or '&'. Takes precedence over a #hashtag in the post content, which then stays plain text. Used only by Threads posts; applies to every post in this call, so use separate calls for different topics. Omit for no topic.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: approve_posts
tools.title: Approve Posts
tools.description: Approve posts so they publish at their scheduled time. This is the only way a post created with create_posts goes out, so show the user exactly what will be posted, where and when, and call this only after they say yes in the conversation, even if they asked you to post it. Can also set PENDING_APPROVAL, REJECTED or NEEDS_WORK. If its scheduled time passed more than 2 hours ago, don't approve it. Tell the user, and only if they agree, create it again with a new time and delete the old one.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: delete_post
tools.title: Delete Post
tools.description: Delete a social media post by id. This removes the post from PostFast — its record, its schedule, and its stored media. It does NOT delete anything from the social platform: a post that has already published stays live there and must be removed on the platform itself. Deleting a SCHEDULED post that has not published yet does prevent it from publishing. Deleting can't be undone, so show the user which post (account, time, first line) and call this only after they say yes in the conversation.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: get_post_analytics
tools.title: Get Post Analytics
tools.description: Fetch published posts with their latest performance metrics (impressions, reach, likes, comments, shares). Only returns published posts that have a platform post ID. LinkedIn personal accounts are excluded. Supported: Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Threads, YouTube, LinkedIn (company pages), Pinterest (Business accounts). Metric counts are returned as strings. Pinterest extras include pin_clicks, outbound_clicks, saves_90d, save_rate_90d (saves are 90-day rolling because Pinterest API does not expose lifetime totals); video pins additionally surface mrc_views, views_10s, avg_watch_time, v50_watch_time, video_starts, quartile_95_views. Video posts also include normalized watch-time on latestMetric: avgWatchTimeSeconds, totalWatchTimeSeconds, videoViews (Facebook, Instagram Reels, YouTube, Pinterest, LinkedIn company pages, TikTok). Instagram posts also include on latestMetric: saveRate (saves / reach as a percentage, rounded to 2 decimals — on IG feed posts, reels, and carousels with metrics) and reelsSkipRate (Instagram Reels only — percentage of viewers who skipped the reel in the first 3 seconds, as reported by Instagram, rounded to 2 decimals; may be absent on low-view reels or until metrics refresh). TikTok also exposes total_time_watched, average_time_watched, and full_video_watched_rate in metric.extras.

socialMediaIds.description: Filter by specific social media account ids

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.title: List Accounts
tools.description: List all social media accounts connected to the workspace. Each account includes connectionStatus (CONNECTED or DISABLED) and disabledReason (null unless DISABLED), plus followerCount (latest stored snapshot, a string; absent for platforms without follower data), followerCountUpdatedAt, and inboxCapable (whether the account can appear in the social inbox, i.e. comment ingestion is supported). A DISABLED account will not publish until the user reconnects it — pre-check before scheduling. For a follower trend over time, use get_follower_history.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_pinterest_boards
tools.title: List Pinterest Boards
tools.description: List Pinterest boards for a connected Pinterest account (pass its socialMediaId). Use a returned board’s boardId field as controls.pinterestBoardId in create_posts.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_youtube_playlists
tools.title: List YouTube Playlists
tools.description: List YouTube playlists for a connected YouTube account (pass its socialMediaId). Use a returned playlist’s playlistId field as controls.youtubePlaylistId in create_posts.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_gbp_locations
tools.title: List Google Business Profile Locations
tools.description: List Google Business Profile locations for a connected GBP account (pass its socialMediaId). Use a returned location’s locationId field as controls.gbpLocationId in create_posts.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: get_follower_history
tools.title: Get Follower History
tools.description: Daily follower-count snapshots for one connected account (pass its socialMediaId from list_accounts). Returns currentFollowerCount, delta (current − first snapshot in range), trackingStartedAt (when PostFast began recording this account), and a series of { capturedAt, followerCount } points. All counts are strings (bigint); currentFollowerCount, delta, and trackingStartedAt may be absent until the account has its first snapshot. Optional from/to bound the range (ISO 8601; default last 90 days, capped at 365). Snapshots are forward-only — no data before trackingStartedAt. Coverage: Facebook Pages, Instagram, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Telegram, LinkedIn company pages, and TikTok. Not available: X, personal Facebook.

from.description: Range start (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z). Defaults to 90 days ago.

to.description: Range end (ISO 8601). Defaults to now; range is capped at 365 days.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: search_places
tools.title: Search Places
tools.description: Search for a place to geotag a post. Pass free text (min 2 chars, e.g. a venue name or address); returns matching places, each with an id that works as BOTH controls.facebookPlaceId (Facebook feed posts) and controls.instagramLocationId (Instagram single-media posts). Only Facebook Pages that carry location data are returned.

query.description: Place search text, min 2 characters (e.g. "eiffel tower")

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: generate_connect_link
tools.title: Generate Connect Link
tools.description: Generate a shareable link for external clients to connect their social accounts to the workspace. Can be scoped to specific platforms and return the user to your own app when done. Email the link (sendEmail) only when the user asks you to and gives the address.

sendEmail.description: Send the link via email. Set it only when the user asks you to and gives the address.

email.description: Recipient email (required when sendEmail is true)

platforms.description: Restrict the link to these platforms, e.g. ["INSTAGRAM"]. Omit to offer all of them. Enforced server-side, so a scoped link cannot connect any other platform.

redirectUrl.description: Where the connect page offers to send the user once connecting finishes, with status, platform, accountId and externalId on the query string, plus accountIds (every account connected, comma-separated) after a Facebook or LinkedIn page step. For Facebook, accountId is the first chosen Page. Must be https (http is accepted only on localhost).

externalId.description: Your own reference for this link, echoed back unchanged on the return URL. Letters, digits and - . _ ~ : @ only.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces this connection can act in. Use a workspace id as the optional workspaceId argument on other tools to operate across multiple workspaces (the default workspace is used when omitted).

tools.name: upload_from_url
tools.title: Upload Media From URL
tools.description: Fetch media from a public https URL and store it for use in create_posts. Returns { media_id, type }; pass an IMAGE or VIDEO media_id as a mediaItems[].key. A CAPTION media_id (an .srt or .vtt caption file) goes in controls.youtubeCaptionKey, never in mediaItems. A DOCUMENT media_id (a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file) goes in controls.linkedinAttachmentKey, never in mediaItems. Use this when the media is already at a public https URL, such as a CDN or hosted image. Redirects are followed (each hop is SSRF-validated); the URL must be public https and within the size limit. For a caption file or a document, link to the file itself; a share page doesn't work. Supported types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime; for caption files application/x-subrip (.srt) and text/vtt (.vtt); for LinkedIn documents application/pdf (.pdf), application/msword (.doc), application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (.docx), application/vnd.ms-powerpoint (.ppt) and application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation (.pptx).

sourceUrl.description: Public https URL of the media to upload

contentType.description: MIME type override. If omitted, the source's Content-Type is used. Set it for a caption file: application/x-subrip for .srt, text/vtt for .vtt. Set it for a document only if the source sends a generic type such as application/octet-stream, e.g. application/pdf for .pdf.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.title: Upload Media
tools.description: Upload an image, video, caption file or document for use in create_posts. If the media is already at a public https URL, use upload_from_url instead. If the user attached or generated the file in this conversation and your app passes files to tools, pass it as `file`; the app fills it in. Otherwise pass the file's bytes as base64 in `data` with its MIME type in `contentType`. Only if you can do neither, ask the user for a public https link and use upload_from_url. Returns { media_id, type }; use an IMAGE or VIDEO media_id as a mediaItems[].key. A CAPTION media_id (an .srt or .vtt caption file) goes in controls.youtubeCaptionKey, never in mediaItems. A DOCUMENT media_id (a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file) goes in controls.linkedinAttachmentKey, never in mediaItems. Supported types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime; for caption files application/x-subrip (.srt) and text/vtt (.vtt); for LinkedIn documents application/pdf (.pdf), application/msword (.doc), application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (.docx), application/vnd.ms-powerpoint (.ppt) and application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation (.pptx).

file.description: The file the user attached or generated in this conversation, for apps that pass files to tools; the app fills it in. If yours doesn't, leave this empty and use data + contentType.

download_url.description: Temporary URL to fetch the file

data.description: Base64-encoded file bytes (alternative to file; no data: prefix)

contentType.description: MIME type for base64 data (e.g. image/png; application/x-subrip for an .srt caption file, text/vtt for a .vtt one; application/pdf for a PDF). Required with data.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_inbox_conversations
tools.title: List Inbox Conversations
tools.description: List comment conversations from the social inbox — comments on your connected accounts' posts, grouped per post, newest activity first. Covers TikTok, Instagram, Facebook Pages, and Threads; an account's inboxCapable flag (from list_accounts) tells you whether comments can flow for it today. Comments arrive within seconds of being posted and only from connect/launch onward (no history backfill). Each conversation carries a server-computed reply capability — canReply, maxReplyLength, windowState, disabledReason — plus unreadCount, status (OPEN | SNOOZED | CLOSED), and assignedToUserId. ALWAYS derive whether and how long you can reply from those fields; never assume platform rules. postPreview carries the post's caption and, when available, its public permalink — use the permalink to link the user to the post on the platform (null on Instagram for now).

socialMediaIds.description: Filter by specific social media account ids (from list_accounts)

assignedToUserId.description: Only conversations assigned to this workspace member

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: get_inbox_conversation
tools.title: Get Inbox Conversation
tools.description: Fetch one inbox conversation by id, including its server-computed reply capability (canReply, maxReplyLength, windowState, disabledReason) — derive reply ability from these fields, never from hardcoded platform rules. postPreview carries the post's caption and, when available, its public permalink — use the permalink to link the user to the post on the platform (null on Instagram for now). Returns null when the conversation does not exist in the workspace.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_inbox_items
tools.title: List Inbox Items
tools.description: List the items of one inbox conversation — the comments and the replies sent to them — oldest first by default (order=DESC for newest first). Items carry direction (INBOUND | OUTBOUND), state (VISIBLE | HIDDEN | DELETED), author info, and on Instagram comments canPrivateReply (eligibility for a private reply through preview_private_reply and send_private_reply). Replies sent from PostFast appear exactly once — no duplicates when the platform reports them back.

order.description: Sort by comment time. Default ASC (oldest first); DESC for newest first.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: get_inbox_unread_count
tools.title: Get Inbox Unread Count
tools.description: Total unread comment count across all inbox conversations in the workspace (the sum of per-conversation unreadCount). Use mark_inbox_conversation_read after presenting a conversation to the user.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: set_inbox_item_state
tools.title: Moderate Inbox Comment
tools.description: Hide a comment from the public on the platform (HIDE) or restore it (UNHIDE). Works on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and Threads and can be reversed. To delete a comment permanently, use preview_comment_deletion, then delete_comment. State changes made on the platform itself sync back to the inbox automatically. Hide or unhide a comment only when the user asks.

Returns up to 100 trending sounds with musicSoundId, name, artist, duration, and preview/thumbnail URLs. Pass a musicSoundId to create_posts as tiktokMusicSoundId to attach that sound to a TikTok photo, carousel or video post. genre takes raw TikTok values like 'POP', 'HIP_HOP/RAP', 'R&B/SOUL', 'K-POP' (invalid values return the full valid list in the error). The list rotates daily — fetch fresh rather than reusing old ids for display. An unknown countryCode returns an empty list. If the API returns tiktokMusic.requiresBusinessApi, the TikTok account needs a one-time reconnect.

Returns a preview and a confirmToken; nothing reaches the platform. Then show the user which comment it is (its author and text) and the exact reply, and wait for their yes in the conversation before calling reply_to_comment, even if they already told you what to write. A reply on Threads can't be removed through PostFast afterwards, so say so in the preview.

Pass its confirmToken with the same itemId and text (and workspaceId, if you used one); anything different is rejected. Call it only after the user has seen the preview and said yes in the conversation. Replies on Threads can't be removed through PostFast. A token expires 15 minutes after the preview and works once. Failures return inbox.* codes (for example replyTooLong, replyNotSupported, rateLimited).

Returns a preview and a confirmToken; nothing is sent. Then show the user which comment it is (its author and text) and the exact message, and wait for their yes in the conversation before calling send_private_reply, even if they already told you what to write.

Call it only after the user has seen the preview and said yes in the conversation. A private reply can't be unsent, and a comment takes only one: a second fails with inbox.privateReplyAlreadySent. A token expires 15 minutes after the preview and works once. Other failures include privateReplyWindowExpired and privateReplyNotSupported.

Returns a preview and a confirmToken; nothing changes. Then show the user which comment it is (its author and text) and that it will be deleted permanently, and wait for their yes in the conversation before calling delete_comment.

Pass its confirmToken with the same itemId (and workspaceId, if you used one); anything different is rejected. Call it only after the user has seen the preview and said yes in the conversation. Deleting can't be undone. A token expires 15 minutes after the preview and works once. Failures return inbox.* codes (for example deleteNotSupported on Threads).

tools.name: delete_posts
tools.title: Delete Posts
tools.description: Delete several social media posts by id in one call (up to 100; use delete_post for a single post). This removes each post from PostFast — its record, its schedule, and its stored media. It does NOT delete anything from the social platform: a post that has already published stays live there and must be removed on the platform itself. Deleting a SCHEDULED post that has not published yet does prevent it from publishing. Returns { deletedIds, notFoundIds }; notFoundIds are the ids that don't exist in this workspace, listed once each. Deleting can't be undone, so show the user every post you are about to delete (account, time, first line) and call this only after they say yes in the conversation.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_webhook_endpoints
tools.title: List Webhook Endpoints
tools.description: List the workspace's webhook endpoints: the URLs where PostFast sends a signed JSON event when a post publishes or fails for good, or when an account connects or disconnects. Oldest first, turned-off ones included. Each has id, url, events, description, active, disabledReason (GONE: its receiver answered 410 Gone; FAILING: its deliveries failed for five days and the workspace owner was emailed; null while it is active, or when a user turned it off), lastSuccessAt and lastFailureAt. The signing secret is never listed: create_webhook_endpoint returns it once. To see what was sent and how the receiver answered, use list_webhook_deliveries. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: get_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Get Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Fetch one webhook endpoint by id, with the fields list_webhook_endpoints gives (never the signing secret). An id that isn't in this workspace, or was deleted, fails with webhook.notFound. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: create_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Create Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Register a webhook endpoint: a URL where PostFast sends a signed JSON POST for every event of the chosen types, { id, type, timestamp, workspaceId, data }, where data.post is a post as list_posts returns it and data.account an account as list_accounts returns it. The endpoint gets these events from the whole workspace, for every account; a receiver that wants one account checks data.post.socialMediaId (or data.post.platform) or data.account.id. A workspace can have 5 active endpoints (turned-off ones don't count); one more fails with webhook.limitReached. The answer is the endpoint plus secret (whsec_…), shown this once: PostFast never returns it again, so give it to the user and tell them to store it in their receiver now (if it is lost, delete the endpoint and create a new one). The receiver checks every delivery with it as Standard Webhooks specifies: the webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers, verified over the raw request body; a Standard Webhooks library such as standardwebhooks does this. A delivery counts when the receiver answers 2xx within 15 seconds; redirects are not followed. Anything else is retried up to 7 more times over about a day (after 5 s, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 4 h, 6 h and 7 h). A 410 Gone answer turns the endpoint off at once, and five days of failures with no success turn it off and email the workspace owner. An event can arrive twice and events can arrive out of order, so the receiver should skip an id it has already handled. Offer test_webhook_endpoint to check the receiver. Use only a URL the user gave you. From then on every such event, with its post or account data, goes to that URL, so show the user the URL and the event types and call this only after they say yes in the conversation. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

url.description: The receiver's URL: https on port 443, with a public hostname that contains a dot (no IP address, no localhost or internal name, no user:password@) and resolves to public addresses; at most 2,048 characters. A URL that breaks a rule fails with webhook.urlNotHttps, webhook.urlPortNotAllowed, webhook.urlHostNotAllowed, webhook.urlPrivateAddress (it resolves to a private address), webhook.urlResolutionFailed (the hostname doesn't resolve) or webhook.invalidUrl.

events.description: Event types to send, each at most once: post.published (a post was published), post.failed (a post failed for good, with the reason in data.post.lastError; never sent for a failure that will still be retried), account.connected (an account was connected or reconnected; data.reconnected is true for a reconnect, and data.externalId carries the connect link's externalId when it had one) and account.disconnected (PostFast paused an account, for example because its access expired or was revoked). webhook.test can't be chosen: only test_webhook_endpoint sends it.

description.description: A note to tell endpoints apart, such as what the receiver is for (max 255 characters)

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: update_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Update Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Change a webhook endpoint: its url, events or description, or turn it off (active false) or back on (active true). Fields you omit keep their value; description null removes the description. A new url follows the rules of create_webhook_endpoint, keeps the same signing secret, and starts the endpoint's failure count afresh. active true turns an endpoint back on, whether PostFast turned it off (disabledReason GONE or FAILING) or a user did, and resets its failure count; it fails with webhook.limitReached when the workspace already has 5 active endpoints. Events that happen while an endpoint is off are never sent to it, not even after it is turned back on. An id that isn't in this workspace fails with webhook.notFound. Returns the updated endpoint. A new url must be one the user gave you. Show the user what will change and call this only after they say yes in the conversation. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

url.description: New receiver URL, under the rules of create_webhook_endpoint

events.description: The event types to send from now on, replacing the current ones (the values create_webhook_endpoint takes)

description.description: New note (max 255 characters), or null to remove it

active.description: false turns the endpoint off; true turns it back on and resets its failure count

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: delete_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Delete Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Delete a webhook endpoint by id. PostFast stops sending to it at once: deliveries still waiting are dropped, and its delivery log and signing secret are deleted with it. To pause an endpoint instead, set active false with update_webhook_endpoint. An id that isn't in this workspace fails with webhook.notFound. Returns { ok: true }. Deleting can't be undone, so show the user which endpoint (its url and description) and call this only after they say yes in the conversation. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: test_webhook_endpoint
tools.title: Test Webhook Endpoint
tools.description: Send one signed test delivery to a webhook endpoint now and report how its receiver answered: { eventId, type, delivered, statusCode, latencyMs, error }. It waits up to 15 seconds for the receiver, and the call succeeds even when the receiver failed, so read delivered, statusCode and error (null when delivered; otherwise timeout, connection, tls, redirect, http_4xx, http_5xx, gone, blocked_address, payload_too_large, or internal, which is PostFast's own failure). Without sampleEvent it sends a webhook.test event, whose data is { webhook: { id, url }, message }. With sampleEvent it sends a fixed sample of that event type, built exactly like a real one so the receiver can be set up before any real event happens: ids of zeros, platform X, the post text "Sample post from PostFast" or the account @sample, and no real post or account data. A test counts like any delivery: it shows in list_webhook_deliveries, a failure adds to the endpoint's failure count, and a 410 Gone answer turns the endpoint off. webhook.disabled means PostFast has webhooks switched off for now, not that this endpoint is off. The receiver may act on a test as on a real event, so send one only when the user asks. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

sampleEvent.description: Send a fixed sample of this event type instead of webhook.test

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.title: List Webhook Deliveries
tools.description: List a webhook endpoint's delivery log, newest first: every delivery to it from the last 30 days, with how the receiver answered. Use it to find out why an event did or didn't arrive. Each row has eventId (evt_…, the webhook-id header the receiver got), eventType, resourceId (the post id for post events, the account id for account events, the endpoint id for webhook.test, null for a sample), status, attempts (each with n, at, statusCode, latencyMs and error), lastStatusCode, lastErrorCode, nextAttemptAt, completedAt and payload (the body exactly as sent). status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED (every attempt failed, the receiver answered 410 Gone, or the event was too large to send), PENDING (still being delivered: a nextAttemptAt in the future means a retry is scheduled, up to 8 attempts over about a day) or SKIPPED (not sent because the endpoint was off when the delivery came due, possibly after failed attempts; while an endpoint is off, its PENDING rows end this way unless it is turned back on before they come due). Error codes: timeout, connection, tls, redirect (redirects are not followed), http_4xx, http_5xx, gone (410), blocked_address (PostFast refused to connect because the hostname resolved to a private address), exhausted, payload_too_large (the event was too large to send) and internal (PostFast's own failure, not the receiver's). Only the receiver's status code is kept, never its response body. totalCount and pageInfo.hasNextPage are filled only when getCount is true, so ask for it on the first page; without it, a full page may have more after it. An id that isn't in this workspace, or was deleted, gives an empty page rather than an error; get_webhook_endpoint tells whether it exists. Only workspace admins can use this tool; for anyone else it fails with webhook.forbidden, which reconnecting doesn't fix.

limit.description: Deliveries per page (max 100; every row carries the full event payload)

getCount.description: Count the whole log, which fills totalCount and pageInfo.hasNextPage. Ask for it on the first page only.

workspaceId.description: Target workspace id (from list_workspaces). Omit to use the connection's default workspace.
